queue.title: F12 (severity A, open) - spec loop: an idle loop must not erase its own history
queue.detail: FULL SPEC LOOP: explore+propose -> review -> review -> implement, as four passes. F12, confirmed live and never fixed: `stop_when_queue_empties` defines empty by TERMINAL_FOR_BINDING = ('approved','rejected') (scheduler.py:91), so a loop whose agent finished every task is NOT empty - the tasks sit `completed` awaiting review. Measured: both tasks completed 17:56, the loop then fired 17:57/17:58/17:59, once a minute, stopping only at 18:00 after a human approved. Overnight that is ~480 firings. Worse, `_prune_job_history` keeps the most recent 100 JobRuns, so at one skip per minute THE RECORD OF THE FIRINGS THAT DID REAL WORK IS DELETED AFTER 100 MINUTES - the loop's idling destroys the evidence of its own work. The skipping itself is CORRECT (`_loop_stall_reason` argues stopping would be unrecoverable); do not 'fix' that. See the pre-authorised direction in decisions_for_user[1].

decisions_for_user: PRE-AUTHORISED - WHAT TO DROP WHEN TIME RUNS OUT. Drop E2E-2 first, then Q4, then F12. Never drop a ROUND from a change you have started, and never leave a change half-proposed. Finish the item you are in, then stop. Dropping the tail is the intended outcome and needs no permission.

PRE-AUTHORISED - F12's DIRECTION, if the spec loop does not find a better one. The defect worth fixing is that idle firings evict the record of real work, not the idling itself. Prefer (a) not letting skip-only JobRuns evict substantive ones from the 100-record window, and (b) bounding or backing off consecutive identical skips so an overnight loop does not fire 480 times. Do NOT make the loop stop on a stalled queue - `_loop_stall_reason` argues correctly that stopping would be unrecoverable, and the operator has not asked for it. If review round 2 or 3 concludes this direction is wrong, SAY SO in the artifacts and stop before implementing rather than building it anyway.

NEW, from iteration 2's sweep - F76's fix shape, severity A and deliberately not guessed. A review turn started by hand (POST /agent/trigger with review_task_id) provisions the reviewer's checkout but never staffs the task, so the reviewer cannot move it (still assigned to its author), cannot accept evidence (no grant), cannot record its own (F75's key), and cannot message the operator (F77). The loop/flow path DOES staff it - scheduler.py:767-780 sets the assignee and applies completed -> under_review before the turn, which is F70's fix. So one operation has two dispatch paths and only one leaves the reviewer able to finish. Three repairs are live: (a) the manual trigger staffs the task the way the scheduler does, matching existing behaviour; (b) the trigger refuses up front when the assignee would block the review, which is the cheapest and spends no tokens on a doomed turn; (c) reviewers get a verdict channel that does not require owning the task, which is the largest and also answers F77. Not chosen here.

NEW, from iteration 2 - whether an agent should be able to address the operator at all (F77). send_message reaches only the roster and 404s on 'Operator'; ask_user blocks and is for questions, so a reviewer with a verdict has nowhere to put it. This deliberately touches the retired question-detection backstop: an explicit notify_operator would not be the product guessing whether prose is addressed to a human, which was the reason that backstop went. Recorded, not decided.
method_reminders: A SPEC LOOP is explore+propose -> review -> review -> implement. Rounds 2 and 3 each independently compare the proposal to the actual code and FIX the proposal. It has found a real defect on four consecutive outings.
Finding defects IS the goal tonight. A sweep that finds nothing has failed, not succeeded. Do not tidy the sweep into a success story.
Every fix carries a test you RAN and WATCHED FAIL without the fix. Mutation-check guards: break the line deliberately and confirm a NAMED test fails.

Targeted per-phase test runs are NOT enough when you touch a migration - run the files that assert the head revision too (test_migrations.py, test_project_persistence.py, test_task_workspace_scheme.py).
The Hub suite takes 14-24 minutes and exceeds the 600s command cap - run it in file chunks or in the background. Do not poll it.
`cd` PERSISTS across Bash calls. Use absolute paths after any cd, or you will run commands in the wrong directory and be told 'no such file'.

The openspec validator reads ONLY THE FIRST PHYSICAL LINE of a requirement for the SHALL/MUST modal. A requirement whose SHALL falls to line 2 fails validation with a confusing error. Measured this evening.
`POST /projects` does not exist - it is POST /projects/open with {"path": ...}. PATCH /projects/{id} is a 405; settings are PUT /projects/{id}/settings.
An ALLOW is recorded nowhere - record_permission_decision persists only refusals. Never infer 'the approver did not run' from an absence of rows. That inference cost three investigations of F52.
ruff is not on PATH in Git Bash - use `py -3.11 -m ruff`. black needs --target-version py311. CI lints src/ hub/ tests/ and blacks src/ hub/hub/ hub/tests/ tests/.
A bash heredoc mangles document prose containing backticks and quotes. Write files with a Python script or the Write tool instead.
CI triggers only on push to master and PRs to it. Your feature branch gets no CI, ever - so the suites you run yourself are the only gate you have.
The Hub API wants 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'. An X-API-Key header returns 'Missing or invalid Authorization header', which reads like a bad key rather than a wrong header name.

Spec routes are at /projects/{id}/project/... - a doubled segment. POST /projects/{id}/documents is a 405. close-exploration, propose and phase take their arguments as QUERY parameters, not a body; phase wants both ?path=&to= and a JSON body.
Path.write_text emits CRLF on Windows. Any test about line endings that uses it compares CRLF against CRLF and passes against the defect - use write_bytes. Cost one round in F73.

A duplicate-evidence test needs the second run's workspace_dir set to a checkout of the same commit, or the two footprints name different shas, no duplicate is possible, and the test passes against the defect. Cost one round in F75.
